source.text: Ἐν ἀρχῇ ἦν ὁ λόγος, καὶ ὁ λόγος ἦν πρὸς τὸν θεόν, καὶ θεὸς ἦν ὁ λόγος.

records.literal_gloss: In beginning was the word, and the word was toward the God, and God was the word.

en.L: In [the] beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
en.B: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God.
en.R: In the beginning the Word was already there. The Word was with God, and the Word was God.

es.L: En [el] principio era el Verbo, y el Verbo estaba con Dios, y el Verbo era Dios.
es.B: En el principio era el Verbo, y el Verbo estaba con Dios, y el Verbo era Dios.
es.R: En el principio, el Verbo ya existía. El Verbo estaba con Dios, y el Verbo era Dios.

sw.L: Katika mwanzo alikuwako Neno, na Neno alikuwa kwa Mungu, na Neno alikuwa Mungu.
sw.B: Mwanzoni alikuwako Neno, na Neno alikuwa pamoja na Mungu, na Neno alikuwa Mungu.
sw.R: Mwanzoni Neno alikuwepo tayari. Neno alikuwa pamoja na Mungu, na Neno alikuwa Mungu.

decisions.reason: The same two words open Genesis 1:1 in the Greek Old Testament. John is retelling creation, so every level keeps the echo.
Key term. In Genesis 1 God creates by speaking, so the rendering should keep the link to God speaking. "Reason" imports Greek philosophy John does not develop.
πρός with the accusative normally means "toward"; here it describes presence and relationship. Where a language's natural word is weaker, the note carries the fuller sense.

ὁ λόγος has the article, so it is the subject. θεός comes first without the article and says what the Word is, without making the Word the same person as "the God" just mentioned. "A god" would contradict John's insistence on one God; "divine" is weaker than the noun.
The imperfect ἦν (was, continuing) contrasts with ἐγένετο (came into being) in verses 3, 6 and 14. Readable makes the contrast explicit.

"La Palabra" shows the link to God's speech more plainly, but it is feminine: verse 2 would need "Esta", and the Word would be "she" until becoming a man in verse 14. "El Verbo" is masculine, is the traditional term (from the Latin Verbum), and keeps the pronouns natural. The glossary explains that it means "the Word". For review by a native speaker.

decisions.choice: era for being or identity; estaba for presence
decisions.reason: Spanish must split one Greek verb into ser and estar. "Era el Verbo" and "era Dios" say what he is; "estaba con Dios" says where he was. The Spanish imperfect also carries the continuing sense of ἦν that English Readable had to add with "already".

"Neno" is the ordinary word for a word and for God's word, so it keeps the link to God speaking in Genesis 1. It is a class 5 noun, which would make it "lilikuwa" (it was); because the Word is a person, it takes the personal agreement "alikuwa" (he was), as Swahili does for nouns naming living beings. For review by a native speaker.

decisions.choice: alikuwako for existence; alikuwa kwa (L) or pamoja na (B, R) for presence; alikuwa for identity
alternatives: alikuwa kwa Mungu at every level
decisions.reason: Swahili splits ἦν three ways: "alikuwako" says the Word existed, "alikuwa ... Mungu" says what he is, and the preposition says where he was. For πρὸς Literal keeps "kwa Mungu" (at God's side, towards God); Balanced and Readable say "pamoja na Mungu" (together with God), which a reader cannot mistake for "by God" or "to God". Readable adds "tayari" (already) where the English Readable adds "already".

source.text: οὗτος ἦν ἐν ἀρχῇ πρὸς τὸν θεόν.

records.literal_gloss: This one was in beginning toward the God.

en.L: This one was in [the] beginning with God.
en.B: He was with God in the beginning.
en.R: He was with God from the very beginning.

es.L: Este estaba en [el] principio con Dios.
es.B: Él estaba con Dios en el principio.
es.R: Desde el principio, {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba con Dios.

sw.L: Huyu alikuwa katika mwanzo kwa Mungu.
sw.B: Yeye alikuwa pamoja na Mungu mwanzoni.
sw.R: Tangu mwanzo kabisa alikuwa pamoja na Mungu.

decisions.reason: Verse 2 repeats verse 1 for emphasis. "He" reads naturally and the person is clear; Literal keeps "This one".

decisions.choice: no deity_pronoun span on Yeye or on the verb prefix
decisions.reason: Swahili marks the subject inside the verb (a-likuwa), and a prefix cannot take a capital. A free pronoun at the start of a sentence is capitalised anyway, as in English. So Swahili has fewer pronoun spans than English; the setting applies to free pronouns and possessives (yeye, wake, lake).

source.text: πάντα δι’ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο, καὶ χωρὶς αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο οὐδὲ ἕν. ὃ γέγονεν

records.literal_gloss: All things through him came into being, and apart from him came into being not even one thing. What has come into being

en.L: All things came into being through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and apart from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} not even one thing came into being that has come into being.
en.B: All things came into being through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and without {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} nothing came into being that has come into being.
en.R: Everything was made through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Nothing that exists was made without {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Todas las cosas llegaron a existir por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y aparte de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no llegó a existir ni una sola cosa de lo que ha llegado a existir.
es.B: Todo llegó a existir por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}; sin {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} no llegó a existir nada de lo que existe.
es.R: Por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} se hizo todo. Nada de lo que existe se hizo sin {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

sw.L: Vitu vyote vilikuja kuwako kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, na bila {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakikuja kuwako hata kitu kimoja kilichokuja kuwako.
sw.B: Vitu vyote vilikuja kuwako kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, na bila {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} hakuna kitu chochote kilichokuja kuwako kati ya vyote vilivyopo.
sw.R: Kila kitu kiliumbwa kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}. Hakuna kitu chochote kilichopo ambacho kiliumbwa bila {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}.

decisions.choice: the clause ends verse 3: nothing came into being that has come into being
alternatives: the clause begins verse 4: what has come into being in him was life
decisions.reason: The manuscripts have no punctuation, so both readings are possible; the SBLGNT itself punctuates the other way, as did several early Christian writers. We follow the reading that most translations use because "what has come into being in him was life" is hard to make sense of. A footnote gives the other reading.
γίνομαι means to come to be, happen or become; it is not the usual word for create. The sense, creation through the Word, is the same either way.

decisions.choice: through him: the one through whom the Father acts
decisions.reason: διά with the genitive names the agent through whom someone acts. The Father creates through the Word.
Plain English for Readable; the meaning decision is unchanged.
"Por él" can mean "by him" as the maker. "Por medio de" keeps the Word as the one through whom the Father acts; the same phrase is used for Moses in verse 17.

decisions.choice: llegó a existir (L, B); se hizo (R)
decisions.reason: Follows the meaning decision; "se hizo" is the plain Spanish for Readable.
"Kwa" can mean through, by, with or to, and "na" would make him the maker on his own. "Kupitia" (through) says he is the one through whom God made everything, as the meaning note has it.

"Kuja kuwako" (come to be) keeps the Greek verb's sense of coming into existence, distinct from "alikuwako" (was) in verse 1. Readable says "kiliumbwa" (was created), as the English Readable says "was made".

source.text: ἐν αὐτῷ ζωὴ ἦν, καὶ ἡ ζωὴ ἦν τὸ φῶς τῶν ἀνθρώπων·

records.literal_gloss: in him life was, and the life was the light of the human beings.

en.L: In {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was life, and the life was the light of {{gender:people|men}}.
en.B: In {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was life, and that life was the light of {{gender:all people|men}}.
en.R: Life itself was in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and that life was the light for {{gender:all people|all men}}.

es.L: En {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba la vida, y la vida era la luz de {{gender:los seres humanos|los hombres}}.
es.B: En {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba la vida, y esa vida era la luz de {{gender:toda la humanidad|los hombres}}.
es.R: En {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} estaba la vida misma, y esa vida era la luz para {{gender:toda la humanidad|todos los hombres}}.

sw.L: Ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kulikuwa na uzima, na uzima ulikuwa nuru ya wanadamu.
sw.B: Ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kulikuwa na uzima, na uzima huo ulikuwa nuru ya watu wote.
sw.R: Uzima wenyewe ulikuwa ndani {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na uzima huo ulikuwa nuru kwa watu wote.

decisions.reason: ἀνθρώπων here means humanity as a whole, so the gender setting applies.
The inclusive default says plainly what the word means; Traditional is one tap away.
Spanish "hombres" is often read as generic, but the inclusive default says it plainly.

"Maisha" is a lifetime or the way one lives; "uzima" is life itself, the word Swahili uses for eternal life, so John's life-words stay one word. "Mwanga" is everyday light; "nuru" is light as a figure of God's presence and truth, which is what John means.

decisions.choice: no gender span: wanadamu (L), watu wote (B, R)
decisions.reason: The English offers "men" as a traditional alternative. Swahili "wanadamu" and "watu" already include men and women, and the only male alternative, "wanaume", means males and would change the meaning. So the Swahili has no gender span here or in verse 9.

source.text: καὶ τὸ φῶς ἐν τῇ σκοτίᾳ φαίνει, καὶ ἡ σκοτία αὐτὸ οὐ κατέλαβεν.

records.literal_gloss: And the light in the darkness shines, and the darkness it not overcame.

en.L: And the light shines in the darkness, and the darkness did not overcome it.
en.B: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has not overcome it.
en.R: The light shines in the darkness, and the darkness has never put it out.

es.L: Y la luz brilla en la oscuridad, y la oscuridad no la venció.
es.B: La luz brilla en la oscuridad, y la oscuridad no la ha vencido.
es.R: La luz brilla en la oscuridad, y la oscuridad nunca ha podido apagarla.

sw.L: Na nuru inang'aa katika giza, na giza halikuishinda.
sw.B: Nuru inang'aa gizani, na giza halijaishinda.
sw.R: Nuru inang'aa gizani, na giza halijawahi kuizima.

decisions.choice: present tense: the light is still shining
decisions.reason: John switches to the present tense here. Every level keeps it.
καταλαμβάνω can mean seize, overpower, or grasp with the mind. John 12:35 uses it of darkness overtaking someone, which supports "overcome". John may intend both senses; the note says so.

decisions.choice: has not / has never put it out
decisions.reason: The aorist looks back on a whole history of opposition; the English perfect expresses a result that still holds. Readable's "put it out" keeps the light-and-darkness image.

decisions.choice: no la ha vencido (B); nunca ha podido apagarla (R)
decisions.reason: Follows the meaning decision and its footnote; Readable keeps the light image.

"Kushinda" (overcome) carries the sense in the meaning note. Literal keeps the simple past; Balanced uses the negative perfect "-ja-" (has not overcome), which goes with the present "inang'aa"; Readable says "has never put it out", as the English Readable does.

source.text: Ἐγένετο ἄνθρωπος ἀπεσταλμένος παρὰ θεοῦ, ὄνομα αὐτῷ Ἰωάννης·

records.literal_gloss: There came a man, sent from God, name to him John.

en.L: There came a man sent from God; [the] name [of] him [was] John.
en.B: There came a man sent from God, whose name was John.
en.R: God sent a man named John.

es.L: Vino un hombre enviado de parte de Dios; [el] nombre [de] él [era] Juan.
es.B: Vino un hombre enviado por Dios, que se llamaba Juan.
es.R: Dios envió a un hombre llamado Juan.

sw.L: Alitokea mtu aliyetumwa kutoka kwa Mungu, jina lake Yohana.
sw.B: Alitokea mtu aliyetumwa na Mungu, jina lake Yohana.
sw.R: Mungu alimtuma mtu mmoja aitwaye Yohana.

decisions.reason: John switches from the imperfect "was" of verses 1-2 (the Word simply was) to Ἐγένετο (John came on the scene). Renderings should keep that contrast.
A specific man is meant, so the gender setting does not apply.
Ἐγένετο brings John onto the scene; "alitokea" (appeared, came on the scene) says that, and contrasts with "alikuwako" (was) used of the Word.

source.text: οὗτος ἦλθεν εἰς μαρτυρίαν, ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός, ἵνα πάντες πιστεύσωσιν δι’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: This one came for testimony, so that he might testify about the light, so that all might believe through him.

en.L: This one came for testimony, in order to testify about the light, so that all might believe through him.
en.B: He came as a witness, to testify about the light, so that through him everyone might believe.
en.R: He came to tell people about the light, so that everyone could believe through his message.

es.L: Este vino para testimonio, para dar testimonio acerca de la luz, a fin de que todos creyeran por medio de él.
es.B: Vino como testigo, para dar testimonio de la luz, a fin de que por medio de él todos creyeran.
es.R: Juan vino a hablarle a la gente acerca de la luz, para que todos creyeran por medio de su mensaje.

sw.L: Huyu alikuja kwa ajili ya ushuhuda, ili ashuhudie kuhusu nuru, ili wote waamini kupitia yeye.
sw.B: Alikuja kama shahidi, ili ashuhudie kuhusu nuru, ili kupitia yeye watu wote waamini.
sw.R: Yohana alikuja kuwaambia watu habari za nuru, ili kila mtu aweze kuamini kupitia ujumbe wake.

decisions.reason: This word family runs through the whole Gospel and carries a courtroom sense. Keep it consistent where the level allows.
The pronoun refers to John: people believe through what he testifies.

source.text: οὐκ ἦν ἐκεῖνος τὸ φῶς, ἀλλ’ ἵνα μαρτυρήσῃ περὶ τοῦ φωτός.

records.literal_gloss: That one was not the light, but so that he might testify about the light.

en.L: That one was not the light, but [he came] in order to testify about the light.
en.B: He himself was not the light; he came to testify about the light.
en.R: John was not the light himself. He came to tell people about the light.

es.L: Aquel no era la luz, sino [vino] para dar testimonio acerca de la luz.
es.B: Él mismo no era la luz; vino para dar testimonio de la luz.
es.R: Juan no era la luz. Vino para hablar de la luz.

sw.L: Yule hakuwa nuru, bali [alikuja] ili ashuhudie kuhusu nuru.
sw.B: Yeye mwenyewe hakuwa nuru; alikuja ili ashuhudie kuhusu nuru.
sw.R: Yohana hakuwa nuru yenyewe. Alikuja kuwaambia watu habari za nuru.

decisions.choice: emphatic: John, as distinct from the light; the second clause has no verb
decisions.reason: ἐκεῖνος is emphatic. The clause after ἀλλ has no main verb; languages that need one supply "he came".
English needs a verb in the second clause.

source.text: ἦν τὸ φῶς τὸ ἀληθινὸν ὃ φωτίζει πάντα ἄνθρωπον ἐρχόμενον εἰς τὸν κόσμον.

records.literal_gloss: It was the true light, which enlightens every human being, coming into the world.

en.L: The true light, which enlightens every {{gender:person|man}}, was coming into the world.
en.B: The true light, who gives light to {{gender:everyone|every man}}, was coming into the world.
en.R: The true light, who gives light to {{gender:everyone|every man}}, was coming into the world.

es.L: La luz verdadera, que alumbra a todo {{gender:ser humano|hombre}}, venía al mundo.
es.B: La luz verdadera, que alumbra a {{gender:todo ser humano|todo hombre}}, venía al mundo.
es.R: La luz verdadera, la que alumbra a {{gender:todos|todo hombre}}, venía al mundo.

sw.L: Nuru ya kweli, inayomwangazia kila mtu, ilikuwa ikija ulimwenguni.
sw.B: Nuru ya kweli, inayomwangazia kila mtu, ilikuwa ikija ulimwenguni.
sw.R: Nuru ya kweli, inayompa kila mtu mwanga, ilikuwa ikija ulimwenguni.

decisions.choice: the light was coming into the world
alternatives: every person who comes into the world
decisions.reason: The participle could agree with the light or with every person. John elsewhere speaks of the light coming into the world (3:19; 12:46), and verses 10-11 describe its arrival. A footnote gives the other reading.
Generic, so the gender setting applies.
"Enlightens" now suggests sudden understanding or the Enlightenment; "gives light to" keeps the image.
Inclusive default; Traditional one tap away.
As in verse 4.

decisions.choice: inayomwangazia: the light keeps its own agreement
decisions.reason: The English Balanced and Readable say "who gives light". In Swahili the verb must agree with "nuru" (i-), and a personal "anaye-" with "nuru" would read as an error. The person comes into view in verse 10, where the verbs turn personal (alikuwa, haukumtambua).

source.text: Ἐν τῷ κόσμῳ ἦν, καὶ ὁ κόσμος δι’ αὐτοῦ ἐγένετο, καὶ ὁ κόσμος αὐτὸν οὐκ ἔγνω.

records.literal_gloss: In the world he was, and the world through him came into being, and the world him did not know.

en.L: In the world {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was, and the world came into being through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and the world did not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He was in the world, and though the world came into being through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, the world did not recognize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: He was in the world. The world was made through {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, but the world did not recognize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: En el mundo estaba, y el mundo llegó a existir por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y el mundo no lo conoció.
es.B: Estaba en el mundo, y aunque el mundo llegó a existir por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, el mundo no lo reconoció.
es.R: Él estaba en el mundo. El mundo fue hecho por medio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, pero el mundo no lo reconoció.

sw.L: Ulimwenguni alikuwako, na ulimwengu ulikuja kuwako kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, na ulimwengu haukumjua.
sw.B: Alikuwa ulimwenguni, na ingawa ulimwengu ulikuja kuwako kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, ulimwengu haukumtambua.
sw.R: Yeye alikuwa ulimwenguni. Ulimwengu uliumbwa kupitia {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}}, lakini ulimwengu haukumtambua.

decisions.choice: failed to acknowledge who he was
decisions.reason: γινώσκω here is refusal to recognise, not ignorance.

decisions.choice: the "and"s carry irony: the world he made did not know him
decisions.reason: John often uses καὶ where the sense is a contrast. Languages that need an explicit contrast should add one.
See the meaning decision.
English needs "though" to carry the irony.

source.text: εἰς τὰ ἴδια ἦλθεν, καὶ οἱ ἴδιοι αὐτὸν οὐ παρέλαβον.

records.literal_gloss: To his own things he came, and his own people him did not receive.

en.L: To {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own [things] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own [people] did not receive {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: He came to what was {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people did not receive {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: He came to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people, but they would not accept {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: A lo suyo vino, y los suyos no lo recibieron.
es.B: Vino a lo que era suyo, y los suyos no lo recibieron.
es.R: Vino a su propio pueblo, pero ellos no lo aceptaron.

sw.B: Alikuja kwa kilicho {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}}, na watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} wenyewe hawakumpokea.
sw.R: Alikuja kwa watu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, lakini wao hawakumkubali.

decisions.choice: his own place; his own people (Israel)
decisions.reason: The first is neuter (his own things, his own place); the second is masculine (his own people). Literal shows the difference; Readable may merge them.

decisions.choice: vilivyo vyake ... walio wake (L); kilicho chake ... watu wake (B)
decisions.reason: Swahili can use a possessive on its own, but "alikuja kwa vyake" is unclear. The class prefixes keep the Greek's two words apart: "vi-" for ἴδια (his own things, his own place) and "wa-" for ἴδιοι (his own people). Literal brackets the supporting "vilivyo", "walio".

source.text: ὅσοι δὲ ἔλαβον αὐτόν, ἔδωκεν αὐτοῖς ἐξουσίαν τέκνα θεοῦ γενέσθαι, τοῖς πιστεύουσιν εἰς τὸ ὄνομα αὐτοῦ, οἳ οὐκ ἐξ αἱμάτων οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος σαρκὸς οὐδὲ ἐκ θελήματος ἀνδρὸς ἀλλ’ ἐκ θεοῦ ἐγεννήθησαν.

records.literal_gloss: But as many as received him, he gave to them authority children of God to become, to the ones believing in his name, \v 13 who not from bloods nor from will of flesh nor from will of a husband but from God were born.

en.L: But as many as received {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them authority to become children of God, to those believing in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, \v 13 who were born not of bloods, nor of [the] will of [the] flesh, nor of [the] will of a husband, but of God.
en.B: But to all who received {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, who believed in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} name, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the right to become children of God— \v 13 children born not of blood, nor of human desire, nor of a husband's will, but born of God.
en.R: But some did accept {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and believe in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. To them {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the right to become God's children. \v 13 They became {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} children not by natural birth, not by human choice, not by a husband's decision, but because God gave them new birth.

es.L: Pero a cuantos lo recibieron, les dio autoridad de llegar a ser hijos de Dios, a los que creen en su nombre, \v 13 los cuales no nacieron de sangres, ni de voluntad de carne, ni de voluntad de varón, sino de Dios.
es.B: Pero a todos los que lo recibieron, a los que creen en su nombre, les dio el derecho de llegar a ser hijos de Dios. \v 13 Estos no nacieron de sangre, ni por deseo humano, ni por voluntad de un esposo, sino que nacieron de Dios.
es.R: Pero a los que sí lo aceptaron y creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, les dio el derecho de ser hijos de Dios. \v 13 Llegaron a ser sus hijos no por nacimiento natural, ni por decisión humana, ni por decisión de un esposo, sino porque Dios los hizo nacer.

sw.L: Lakini wote waliompokea, aliwapa mamlaka ya kuwa watoto wa Mungu, wale wanaoamini katika jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, \v 13 ambao hawakuzaliwa kutokana na damu, wala kutokana na mapenzi ya mwili, wala kutokana na mapenzi ya mume, bali kutokana na Mungu.
sw.B: Lakini wote waliompokea, wale wanaoliamini jina {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}, aliwapa mamlaka ya kuwa watoto wa Mungu. \v 13 Hawa hawakuzaliwa kwa damu, wala kwa tamaa ya kibinadamu, wala kwa mapenzi ya mume, bali walizaliwa na Mungu.
sw.R: Lakini wengine walimpokea na kumwamini. Hao aliwapa uwezo wa kuwa watoto wa Mungu. \v 13 Hawakuwa watoto {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} kwa kuzaliwa kimwili, wala kwa uamuzi wa binadamu, wala kwa uamuzi wa mume, bali kwa sababu Mungu ndiye aliyewazaa.

decisions.reason: The word means a right given, not an ability.

decisions.choice: children of God, of either sex
decisions.reason: τέκνα is neuter and already inclusive, so the gender setting does not apply.
In Hebrew thought a name stands for the person.
Spanish "hijos" is the ordinary word for children of both sexes. Adding "e hijas" would add words the Greek does not have.
The plural is an idiom for physical descent. Being born a Jew does not make someone God's child.
σάρξ here means ordinary human nature, not sinful nature as in Paul.
ἀνήρ is male; in a sentence about conception it means the husband. The gender setting does not apply.

alternatives: singular "who was born", referring to Christ
decisions.reason: The singular has only weak, mainly Latin, support. We follow the Greek manuscripts; a footnote names the variant because it changes who is meant.
Spanish has a word for male, "varón", which Literal uses to keep the distinction. Balanced and Readable follow the meaning decision.

"Haki" is the usual word for a right, but it is the settled word for righteousness, so it is kept for that. "Mamlaka" (authority) says a granted right; Readable says "uwezo" (the power, the means) as simpler Swahili.

The English Readable says "God gave them new birth". "Ndiye aliyewazaa" (it is God who gave them birth) is the plain Swahili for the same thing and keeps the contrast with the three ways they were not born.

source.text: Καὶ ὁ λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο καὶ ἐσκήνωσεν ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ἐθεασάμεθα τὴν δόξαν αὐτοῦ, δόξαν ὡς μονογενοῦς παρὰ πατρός, πλήρης χάριτος καὶ ἀληθείας·

records.literal_gloss: And the word flesh became and pitched his tent among us, and we beheld his glory, glory as of an only one from a father, full of grace and truth.

en.L: And the Word became flesh and tabernacled among us, and we beheld {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, glory as of [the] one and only [Son] from [the] Father, full of grace and truth.
en.B: The Word became flesh and made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home among us. We have seen {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, the glory of the one and only Son from the Father, full of grace and truth.
en.R: The Word became a human being and lived among us. We saw {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory, the glory of the Father's one and only Son, full of grace and truth.

es.L: Y el Verbo se hizo carne y acampó entre nosotros, y contemplamos su gloria, gloria como del unigénito del Padre, lleno de gracia y de verdad.
es.B: El Verbo se hizo carne e hizo su morada entre nosotros. Hemos visto su gloria, la gloria del Hijo único que viene del Padre, lleno de gracia y de verdad.
es.R: El Verbo se hizo hombre y vivió entre nosotros. Vimos su gloria, la gloria del Hijo único del Padre, lleno de gracia y de verdad.

sw.L: Na Neno akawa mwili, akapiga hema kati yetu, na tukautazama utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, utukufu kama wa [Mwana] wa pekee kutoka kwa Baba, amejaa neema na kweli.
sw.B: Neno akawa mwili, akafanya makao {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kati yetu. Tumeuona utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, utukufu wa Mwana wa pekee aliyetoka kwa Baba, akiwa amejaa neema na kweli.
sw.R: Neno akawa binadamu, akaishi pamoja nasi. Tuliuona utukufu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}, utukufu wa Mwana wa pekee wa Baba, aliyejaa neema na kweli.

alternatives: took on the appearance of a body
decisions.reason: The phrase is deliberately blunt: the eternal Word became fully human. Literal and Balanced keep the original image; Readable may say what it means.

decisions.choice: lived among us as God's glory lived in the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The verb means to live in a tent and recalls the tabernacle, where God's glory dwelt among Israel (Exodus 25:8; 40:34). The next words, about seeing his glory, complete the picture.
We looked at him ourselves (compare 1 John 1:1).
μονογενής is built from μόνος (only) and γένος (kind), not from γεννάω (beget); Hebrews 11:17 uses it of Isaac, who was not Abraham's only son. "Only begotten" came through the Latin unigenitus.

decisions.choice: full of grace and truth (key term: grace)
alternatives: full of unfailing love and faithfulness
decisions.reason: Probably echoes God's self-description in Exodus 34:6, abounding in steadfast love and faithfulness (Hebrew hesed and emet). "Grace" stays a key term; the note gives the Exodus link.
Greek leaves the noun unstated, but "from the Father" and John 3:16, 18 make "Son" clear.
"Acampó" keeps the tent image for Literal; "morada" recalls the dwelling of God's glory.
Jesus is a specific man, so the gender rule does not apply; "se hizo hombre" is also the phrase of the Nicene Creed in Spanish.
In today's Spanish "unigénito" just means an only child, so Literal may use it. Balanced and Readable avoid it because "-génito" suggests "begotten", the reading the meaning decision rejects.

decisions.choice: akapiga hema (L); akafanya makao yake (B); akaishi (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the picture of pitching a tent, which points to the tabernacle; Balanced says he made his dwelling among us; Readable says simply that he lived with us.
"Akawa mwili" (became flesh) can read in Swahili as "became a body". Readable says "binadamu" (a human being), as the English Readable says "a human being".

"Neema" is grace at every level. For truth, "kweli" is the older noun and still standard, and it is also the adjective "true" in verse 9 (nuru ya kweli), keeping John's link between them. "Ukweli" is the everyday modern noun; a native reviewer may prefer it, at least at Readable.

source.text: Ἰωάννης μαρτυρεῖ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ κέκραγεν λέγων· Οὗτος ἦν ὃν εἶπον· Ὁ ὀπίσω μου ἐρχόμενος ἔμπροσθέν μου γέγονεν, ὅτι πρῶτός μου ἦν·

records.literal_gloss: John testifies about him and has cried out saying, "This was he whom I said: 'The one after me coming ahead of me has become, because first of me he was.'"

en.L: John testifies about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and has cried out, saying, "This was {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} of whom I said, 'The one coming after me has come to be ahead of me, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was before me.'"
en.B: John testified about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and cried out, "This is the one I meant when I said, 'He who comes after me ranks ahead of me, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} existed before me.'"
en.R: John told people about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He shouted, "This is the one I was talking about! I said, 'Someone is coming after me who is greater than I am, because {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} existed before me.'"

es.L: Juan da testimonio acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y ha clamado diciendo: «Este era aquel de quien dije: “El que viene después de mí ha llegado a estar delante de mí, porque era antes que yo”».
es.B: Juan dio testimonio de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y exclamó: «Este es aquel de quien yo dije: “El que viene después de mí es superior a mí, porque existía antes que yo”».
es.R: Juan habló de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} a la gente. Gritó: «¡Este es de quien yo hablaba! Dije: “Viene alguien después de mí que es más importante que yo, porque existía antes que yo”».

sw.L: Yohana anashuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, naye amepaza sauti akisema, "Huyu alikuwa ndiye niliyesema habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}: 'Anayekuja nyuma yangu amekuwa mbele yangu, kwa sababu alikuwa kabla yangu.'"
sw.B: Yohana alishuhudia habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}, akapaza sauti, "Huyu ndiye niliyesema habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}: 'Anayekuja baada yangu ni mkuu kuliko mimi, kwa sababu alikuwako kabla yangu.'"
sw.R: Yohana aliwaambia watu habari {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}. Alipaza sauti, "Huyu ndiye niliyekuwa nikimzungumzia! Nilisema, 'Anakuja mtu baada yangu aliye mkuu kuliko mimi, kwa sababu alikuwepo kabla yangu.'"

decisions.reason: "Ahead" here means rank, not time.
John the Baptist was born before Jesus (Luke 1). The claim is that Jesus existed before John, which picks up verses 1-2.
The present and perfect present John's testimony as still standing; English narrative needs the past.
Standard Spanish typography for a quotation within a quotation.
"Kumsema mtu" means to speak against someone. "Kusema habari za" (to speak about) is the neutral Swahili.

source.text: ὅτι ἐκ τοῦ πληρώματος αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς πάντες ἐλάβομεν, καὶ χάριν ἀντὶ χάριτος·

records.literal_gloss: Because from his fullness we all received, and grace for grace.

en.L: Because from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fullness we all received, even grace for grace.
en.B: From {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fullness we have all received grace upon grace.
en.R: Out of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fullness we have all received one gift of grace after another.

es.L: Porque de su plenitud todos nosotros recibimos, y gracia por gracia.
es.B: De su plenitud todos hemos recibido gracia sobre gracia.
es.R: De su plenitud todos hemos recibido un regalo de gracia tras otro.

sw.L: Kwa sababu kutoka katika utimilifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} sisi sote tulipokea, hata neema badala ya neema.
sw.B: Kutoka katika utimilifu {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} sisi sote tumepokea neema juu ya neema.
sw.R: Kutoka katika wingi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} sote tumepokea zawadi moja ya neema baada ya nyingine.

decisions.choice: grace upon grace: one gift following another
alternatives: grace in place of grace: the grace in Christ replacing the grace given through the law
decisions.reason: ἀντί usually means "in place of", which supports the alternative and fits verse 17. We chose accumulation because verse 17 does not call the law grace. Literal may keep the open "grace for grace": a level may keep an ambiguity the original has, but may not pick the other side.
No change of meaning, so no footnote.

decisions.choice: utimilifu (L, B); wingi (R); badala ya (L); juu ya (B)
decisions.reason: "Utimilifu" is fullness; "ukamilifu" means perfection, which is not the point. Readable says "wingi" (abundance) as the plainer word. Literal translates ἀντὶ as "badala ya" (in place of); Balanced gives the sense in the meaning note, one gift on top of another.

source.text: ὅτι ὁ νόμος διὰ Μωϋσέως ἐδόθη, ἡ χάρις καὶ ἡ ἀλήθεια διὰ Ἰησοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐγένετο.

records.literal_gloss: Because the law through Moses was given; the grace and the truth through Jesus Christ came.

en.L: Because the law was given through Moses; the grace and the truth came through Jesus {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}.
en.B: For the law was given through Moses; grace and truth came through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.
en.R: God gave the law through Moses. Grace and truth came through Jesus {{christos:Christ|the Messiah}}.

es.L: Porque la ley fue dada por medio de Moisés; la gracia y la verdad vinieron por medio de Jesús {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}.
es.B: Porque la ley fue dada por medio de Moisés; la gracia y la verdad vinieron por medio de Jesús {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.
es.R: Dios dio la ley por medio de Moisés. La gracia y la verdad vinieron por medio de Jesús {{christos:Cristo|el Mesías}}.

sw.L: Kwa sababu sheria ilitolewa kupitia Musa; neema na kweli zilikuja kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.B: Kwa maana sheria ilitolewa kupitia Musa; neema na kweli zilikuja kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.
sw.R: Mungu alitoa sheria kupitia Musa. Neema na kweli zilikuja kupitia Yesu {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}.

decisions.choice: law and grace side by side, not opposed
decisions.reason: John puts the two clauses side by side with no "but". The law was given, which is also a gift; a contrast word would set law against grace more sharply than John does.
The first time John's Gospel names Jesus. The word is a title, "anointed one" (John 1:41 explains it).
As in English.
Swahili has no article, so "Yesu Masihi" reads as naturally as "Yesu Kristo" at every level, where the English needs "the Messiah".

source.text: θεὸν οὐδεὶς ἑώρακεν πώποτε· μονογενὴς θεὸς ὁ ὢν εἰς τὸν κόλπον τοῦ πατρὸς ἐκεῖνος ἐξηγήσατο.

records.literal_gloss: God no one has seen ever; only-one God, the one being into the bosom of the Father, that one has explained.

en.L: No one has ever seen God; [the] one and only God, the one being in the bosom of the Father, that one has made [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] known.
en.B: No one has ever seen God. The one and only Son, who is {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} God and is close beside the Father, has made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} known.
en.R: No one has ever seen God. But the one and only Son, who is {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} God and is closest to the Father, has shown us what God is like.

es.L: A Dios nadie lo ha visto jamás; [el] unigénito Dios, el que está en el seno del Padre, ese lo ha dado a conocer.
es.B: Nadie ha visto jamás a Dios. El Hijo único, que es {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo Dios y está al lado del Padre, lo ha dado a conocer.
es.R: Nadie ha visto jamás a Dios. Pero el Hijo único, que es {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} mismo Dios y está más cerca del Padre que nadie, nos ha mostrado cómo es Dios.

sw.L: Mungu hakuna aliyewahi kumwona; Mungu wa pekee, aliye kifuani mwa Baba, huyo amemtambulisha.
sw.B: Hakuna mtu aliyewahi kumwona Mungu. Mwana wa pekee, ambaye {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} mwenyewe ni Mungu, na yuko karibu kabisa na Baba, ndiye aliyemtambulisha.
sw.R: Hakuna mtu aliyewahi kumwona Mungu. Lakini Mwana wa pekee, ambaye {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} mwenyewe ni Mungu, na aliye karibu zaidi na Baba, ametuonyesha jinsi Mungu alivyo.

alternatives: the one and only Son (most later manuscripts)
decisions.reason: "God" has the oldest witnesses (the papyri P66 and P75, Codex Sinaiticus and Codex Vaticanus) and is the harder reading, which scribes were more likely to change to the familiar "Son". A footnote gives "Son".
Diners reclined so that one rested against another's chest (John 13:23). The image is intimacy.

decisions.choice: has made him known, explained him
decisions.reason: The verb, from which "exegesis" comes, means to lead out, explain, narrate. The Son reveals the God no one has seen.

decisions.choice: The one and only Son, who is himself God
decisions.reason: "The only God" would suggest the Father is not God. Supplying "Son", as in verse 14, keeps both truths.
As in verse 14.

decisions.choice: amemtambulisha, with the object in the verb
decisions.reason: The English Literal brackets "[him]", which the Greek leaves out. Swahili puts the object inside the verb (-m-), so it cannot be bracketed or left out; "amemtambulisha" (has made him known) is the nearest Literal can come.
